html:
Around 380 the kings of Himyar, who ruled all of Yemen from their capital at Zafar, turned from the old gods to the worship of one God, and the ruling elite adopted Judaism.

Himyar had united southern Arabia after Saba. Its kings stood between the Christian Roman world and Aksum on one side and Persia on the other. Around 523 the Jewish king Dhu Nuwas killed many Christians at Najran, and the Christian king of Aksum answered by invading (Aksum invades Yemen).

The Aksumite general Abraha then ruled Yemen, and in 570 Persia took it. A Jewish community lived on in Yemen until most of its members left for Israel around 1949 and 1950.
sum: Around 380 the kings of Himyar, who ruled all of Yemen from their capital at Zafar, turned from the old gods to the worship of one God, and the ruling elite adopted Judaism.
